messages:
maya: dropping a compact prototype for the latency overview. two big changes: 1) move the global sampling control inline with the time picker, 2) make the legend a floating overlay instead of inline. Fig: https://figma.com/file/abc (preview)

ron: nice! quick thought: floating legend could occlude the heatmap on small screens. can it dock to the right on wide screens and collapse into a button on narrow ones?

maya: yes — responsive plan: dock right >= 1200px, overlay center for 900-1200, collapse to an icon that opens a panel <900. will add specs.

eli: on sampling placement: putting it next to time picker is great for discoverability. can we add an optional preset dropdown (low/medium/high) for quick selection? technical folks still want % input for precision though.

sarah: microcopy: avoid the word "sampling" alone. suggest label: "Capture rate (requests)" and helper: "Higher = more accurate p95, higher cost". keeps product folks from misreading.

eli: accessibility note: the mini dropdown and % input must be accessible as one composite control, screen readers should announce both and the current combined value.

a11y-bot: checklist: 1) composite control role=group with aria-label="Capture rate control". 2) ensure value announcements on change. 3) preset buttons keyboard-focusable and have aria-pressed states.

ron: heatmap binning question: current heatmap shows 1-min bins. for long ranges that creates too many cells. can we auto-aggregate bins by zoom/time-range (e.g., 1-min <24h, 5-min 1-7d, 1h >7d)? also show bin size in the top-left of the heatmap.

maya: agreed. i'll add a small label: "bin: 5m" and a tooltip: "Aggregation window used to compute cell values".

eli: legend ordering: request to surface the most-used metrics first (p95, throughput, error-rate). can we make the legend sort adaptive by frequency of viewing (local per-user)? but then the order changes and could confuse folks. maybe a toggle: "smart order" vs "fixed order".

sarah: prefer fixed order with a small "sort by usage" option in settings. cognitive load if it jumps around.

maya: ok — default fixed order, opt-in smart order. will stub the settings flag.

ron: visual affordance: when a legend item is toggled off, reduce heatmap saturation for that metric's cells and add a tiny faded chip in the legend row showing sample count. helps correlate visibility with data volume.

eli: implementation: careful about reruns on toggle. suggest client-side mask + background refetch only on time-range change or sampling change. also include an optimistic preview (fade) while background refetch resolves.

a11y-bot: note: faded chips still need readable labels. ensure contrast and provide text alternatives: e.g., "route /chat — 12k samples".

sarah: copy for presets and helper tips: presets: "Low (5%) — cost-saving, good for long trends", "Medium (20%) — balanced", "High (80%) — full fidelity". helper under timepicker: "Tip: increase capture rate for windows >30d to preserve trend visibility".

maya: saving these strings into the handoff doc. also adding sample analytic events: `latency.capture.change`, `heatmap.bin.change`, `legend.item.toggle`. payload examples in spec.

ron: one more UX flow: focus mode. clicking a legend item should be able to enter a focused view that isolates that metric and stretches the heatmap y-axis to show fine-grained changes. should be reversible with Esc.

eli: +1 for Esc to exit. ensure focus trapping in the floating legend panel while open.

a11y-bot: focus trap guidelines: 1) trap only for modal panels, 2) restore focus to trigger element on close, 3) provide an accessible label and close button.

deploy-bot: FYI: staging deploy scheduled for design assets -> staging on 2026-04-02T02:00:00Z

maya: thanks team — I'll update the Figma file with responsive legend behaviors, capture rate composite control, and all microcopy. will post the final handoff here by tomorrow afternoon and attach a small prototype for keyboard flows.
